Randomized tests for vinyl I/O append, copy, read, commit, sync, forget, and rewind.

# Purpose
This file implements a randomized unit test for `fd_vinyl_io_t`. It compares the behavior of the `fd_vinyl_io` API against a local reference model built on the `bcache` array and the sequence markers `seq_ancient`, `seq_past`, `seq_present`, and `seq_future`. The test checks `fd_vinyl_io_append`, `fd_vinyl_io_copy`, `fd_vinyl_io_commit`, `fd_vinyl_io_hint`, `fd_vinyl_io_forget`, `fd_vinyl_io_rewind`, `fd_vinyl_io_sync`, `fd_vinyl_io_read_imm`, `fd_vinyl_io_read`, and `fd_vinyl_io_poll` under many random operation orders and sizes.

The helper functions [`bcache_read`](<#bcache_read>), [`bcache_append`](<#bcache_append>), [`bcache_copy`](<#bcache_copy>), [`bcache_commit`](<#bcache_commit>), [`bcache_hint`](<#bcache_hint>), [`bcache_forget`](<#bcache_forget>), [`bcache_rewind`](<#bcache_rewind>), and [`bcache_sync`](<#bcache_sync>) model the expected state changes of the I/O object. The [`test`](<#test>) function runs one million random steps, verifies that the sequence state in `io` matches the reference state after each step, and checks that read data and returned values match. The file also contains `FD_STATIC_ASSERT( FD_VINYL_IO_FLAG_BLOCKING==1, unit_test )`, which confirms the expected flag value for blocking I/O in this test.
